candidates.name: gowalla-dataset-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Example code for handling the SNAP/Stanford Gowalla check-in dataset (the standard public release: ~6.4M check-ins from ~200k users worldwide, Feb 2009-Oct 2010, lat/lon + timestamp + user + spot id, hosted at snap.stanford.edu/data/loc-gowalla.html). Repo itself just parses/loads it; no new data collected.
candidates.why_useful: Global geotagged check-in data with lat/lon and time could in principle be turned into a travel/mobility-flow proxy (gap 20: party size/group travel/cross-border proxies via geotagged datasets), but the underlying SNAP dataset only covers 2009-2010, more than a decade before the ABNB forecast window, with no continuation - a historical curiosity, not a usable nowcast input.
candidates.license: none declared in this wrapper repo

candidates.name: gowalla-exp
candidates.what_it_holds: Trajectory-based analysis/experiment code over the same SNAP Gowalla check-in dataset described above; no new data, method/analysis scripts only.
candidates.why_useful: Same underlying 2009-2010 global check-in dataset as above; provides trajectory-extraction code that could be reused if a fresher check-in-style dataset were ever found, but stale on its own.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same source dataset as b00040611/gowalla-dataset-analysis above

candidates.name: LocationEntropy
candidates.what_it_holds: Location-entropy experiments over the SNAP Gowalla dataset; a small academic-style repo with the analysis code, not a new dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal - illustrates a mobility/entropy method applicable to any check-in panel, but tied to the same 2009-2010 Gowalla data.

candidates.name: foursquare-exp
candidates.what_it_holds: Trajectory-based experiment code over a Foursquare check-in dataset (not the full TIST2015 global release found in this pass - appears to be a smaller/older Foursquare check-in sample used in the associated academic paper). No dataset files committed in the repo listing shown; points to an external check-in corpus.
candidates.why_useful: Same category as the Gowalla repos: check-in mobility data that could proxy travel flow/POI popularity if a recent, geographically broad vintage existed; this one's vintage/scope is unclear from the README summary alone and was not independently verified beyond the search snippet.
candidates.geography: unclear from listing (city-level Foursquare check-ins, likely US-centric per typical academic Foursquare samples)
candidates.time_coverage: unclear, pre-2015 based on repo age

candidates.name: preprocessingDatasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Preprocessing scripts for both the Gowalla and Brightkite SNAP check-in datasets (Brightkite: ~4.5M check-ins, ~58k users, Apr 2008-Oct 2010, global). No data files committed, just cleaning/parsing code for the two external datasets.
candidates.why_useful: Convenience tooling for pulling in two of the classic geotagged social check-in corpora at once; both datasets are 2008-2010 vintage and stale for a 2026 nowcast, but the parsing code lowers the cost of exploring them if a team member wants a historical mobility baseline.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same two source datasets as the Gowalla repos above

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub relative to other alt-data themes. Direct keyword searches for 'yfcc100m tourism', 'geotagged tweets tourism', 'flickr geotagged photos tourism', 'foursquare TIST', and 'foursquare NYC check-in' all returned zero gh search results (gh search repos text-matches README/description/topics, not full content, so YFCC100M-derived tourism subsets and geotagged-tweet tourism-flow papers with GitHub companions may exist but aren't surfacing on these terms — a `gh search code` pass for 'YFCC100M' or a Google Dataset Search / paperswithcode crawl would likely do better than gh search repos for this theme). The only repos that surfaced are recsys/ML-benchmark wrappers around three well-known, static, 2008-2010-vintage social check-in corpora (SNAP Gowalla, SNAP Brightkite, an older Foursquare sample) — real geotagged mobility data in principle, but 15+ years stale and never updated, so none of them clear a 'high' or 'medium' potential bar for an ABNB 2026 nowcast; recorded as low-potential provenance notes only. WebSearch could not be used to cross-check (session WebSearch budget of 200 was already exhausted by other agents/session activity before this scout's second tool call). Recommend a follow-up scout try `gh search code "YFCC100M" tourism`, `gh search topics geotagged-photos`, and a non-GitHub Dataset Search sweep (Kaggle/Zenodo/Harvard Dataverse) for TIST2015 Foursquare (global, 2012-2013, ~33M check-ins, 415 cities — genuinely relevant if found with a repo wrapper) and any YFCC100M geo-subset paired with tourism/POI labels, since none of that surfaced here.
